subject: Renewal: MSA + order form redlines for capacity uplift
messages:
From: Talia Green <talia.green@edgestream.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Reddy <samir@edgestream.ai>
Date: 2026-09-27T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal + capacity uplift — initial redlines attached

Hey Dylan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We reviewed the proposed 18-month renewal and the +30% capacity uplift internally. Attached are three items: our redline to the MSA (MSA_v4_redline.pdf), a version of the order form with updated seat/throughput numbers (OrderForm_Q3_2026.xlsx), and a short Exhibit D that scopes logging/retention for our security team (Exhibit_D_draft.docx).

Key asks from our side: 
- Keep liability cap at 1x annual fees (we noted your counter in the MSA but want to preserve this)
- Clarify SLA credits mechanism for burst capacity (we need a deterministic formula)
- Add a 90-day ramp credit if throughput targets aren't met during first month after go-live

Looping in our legal team (legal@edgestream.ai) — expect some inline comments. Can you confirm who from Redwood Legal will own the redline review? Also, we prefer DocuSign for signature.

Cheers,
Talia
Head of Product, EdgeStream

Attachments: MSA_v4_redline.pdf (redline), OrderForm_Q3_2026.xlsx (capacity numbers), Exhibit_D_draft.docx (security scoping)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Talia Green <talia.green@edgestream.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-27T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity uplift — initial redlines attached

Talia — thanks for sending these. We appreciate the clear asks. Quick responses inline: 

- Liability cap: I won't promise changes here without legal sign-off, but we can escalate. Irene (cc) will take point on liability and the liability-cap language.
- SLA credits for burst capacity: we have an internal formula we can propose (credits by excess latency * percent of burst time). Marissa will propose the exact wording for the order form so it's deterministic.
- 90-day ramp credit: OK to discuss — is EdgeStream proposing this as a dollar credit or token/throughput credit? Please confirm preference.

Action plan: 
1) Irene to review MSA redline and call out non-starters or alternative language by EOD 9/28.
2) Marissa to update order form language and produce a clean with tracked changes by 9/29.
3) Neha (CS) to draft ramp credit mechanics for product/ops so we can quantify impact.

I'll anticipate legal comments back to you next week. If you prefer, we can set a 30-min call with legal and CS on Friday.

Best,
Dylan
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-09-28T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal + capacity uplift — MSA redlines attached

Hi Talia / Samir — Irene from Legal here. Thanks for the redlines; I reviewed MSA_v4_redline.pdf and flagged a few areas that need alignment. Summary of our position: 

1) Liability cap: Redwood's standard is 3x fees or $5M (whichever is lower) for renewals of this scale. We are not able to accept 1x annual fees as written. Alternate ask: can EdgeStream agree to a 2x cap for the uplift period only (months 1–12 of the new term)? If not, please provide examples of commercial constraints that require 1x.

2) SLA credits: We can accept a deterministic formula. Proposed wording: "SLA credit = (Monthly fee) * min(0.5, (Aggregate minutes of unavailability during measured burst windows) / (Total scheduled burst minutes))" — detailed example attached in Exhibit_D_draft.docx. Marissa will put a friendly explanation into the order form.

3) Ramp credit: We can offer a ramp credit equal to 15% of monthly invoice for the first month if throughput targets are not met, or a one-time $25k credit — whichever is more useful. Neha, please confirm operational metrics we should tie the ramp to (P95 latency, successful requests/minute, etc.).

Non-starters / asks for redlines: certain audit/logging retention language in your Exhibit D would require us to host additional logs for longer retention; that's an ops cost. If EdgeStream retains the current 90-day log window but accepts a compliance report subscription, that might bridge the ask.

Next steps: 
- EdgeStream to confirm whether 1x liability is dealbreaker.
- Dylan/Marissa to accept SLA credit wording or propose edits by 9/29.
- Neha and Talia to align on the ramp metric (Neha: pls propose a short checklist).

Happy to jump on a call Friday 9/30 — I'm available 10:00-11:30 PT.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment references: inline comments in MSA_v4_redline.pdf; Exhibit_D_draft.docx with SLA examples
From: Samir Reddy <samir@edgestream.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Talia Green <talia.green@edgestream.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: MSA + order form redlines for capacity uplift

Thanks, Irene — quick answers from EdgeStream: 
- Liability cap: 1x is preferred because our procurement team cannot sign above 1x without CFO approval. If Redwood can accept 2x for the uplift period as a compromise, we can spin this up internally to get faster approval. Please consider 2x as meet-me-in-the-middle.
- Ramp credit mechanics: EdgeStream prefers a throughput-based safety net (successful requests per minute at 95th percentile) rather than a pure latency metric. The goal is to ensure baseline capacity while we complete our integration.
- Exhibit D: We are willing to relax the retention to 90 days if Redwood will provide a monthly attest report on access logs for a year.

If those positions are acceptable, we can mark the MSA as ready for DocuSign and push signature this week. Sending our procurement tracker (proc_tracker.xlsx) offline.

Best,
Samir
VP Engineering, EdgeStream
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Talia Green <talia.green@edgestream.ai>, Samir Reddy <samir@edgestream.ai>

Date: 2026-09-30T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: FINAL: Agreement on core points + next steps to signature

Talia / Samir — great progress. Short summary and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Agreed items: 
- Liability cap: Redwood legal to accept 2x annual fees for the first 12 months of the renewed term (=> amendment in MSA Section 10).
- SLA credits: Irene/Marissa to include the deterministic formula in the order form. Example numbers will be added to Exhibit D for clarity.
- Ramp credit: EdgeStream preference noted (throughput P95). Neha to provide the exact throughput threshold by 10/1; Redwood will map to either 15% invoice credit or $25k one-time credit based on measured shortfall.
- Exhibit D: Redwood to provide monthly access-log attest for 12 months in exchange for 90-day retention.

Next steps and timeline: 
1) Marissa to post a clean MSA (MSA_v4_clean.pdf) and updated OrderForm_Q3_2026_clean.xlsx with tracked changes accepted by 10/1.
2) Irene to finalize the liability amendment language and publish redline-ready MSA by 10/1 EOD.
3) Dylan to send DocuSign envelope once clean docs posted (expect to send 10/2).
4) Samir/Talia to confirm procurement sign-off ETA (Samir: you said you could escalate for faster turnaround).

DocuSign link (placeholder) and HubSpot deal updated once envelope is sent. We will push billing/invoice effective date to align with signature date and will confirm billing proration details in the DocuSign package.

If that captures everything, I will close this thread and open a short ops ticket for the ramp-monitoring implementation with Neha.

Thanks all — almost done!

Dylan
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
